questions.q: The legal blood alcohol limit for driving in the UAE is:
options: Same as many Western countries (a small allowed limit)
Zero tolerance - any detectable alcohol is illegal
Only enforced for professional drivers
questions.explanation: Dubai enforces zero tolerance for drink driving: the RTA Light Motor Vehicle Handbook states that driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs is not permitted at all, with no allowance for any detectable amount.

questions.q: Driving while fatigued is dangerous mainly because it:
options: Has no measurable effect on driving
Slows reaction time and can cause microsleeps, similar to impaired driving
Only affects long-distance truck drivers
Improves focus on monotonous roads
questions.explanation: Fatigue slows reactions and can cause brief involuntary microsleeps, making it comparable in risk to alcohol impairment.

questions.q: If you feel drowsy while driving on a long highway trip, you should:
options: Open the window and continue driving
Increase speed to reach the destination sooner
Stop at a safe place to rest before continuing
Drink more coffee and keep driving without stopping
questions.explanation: The safest response to drowsiness is to stop in a safe location and rest, not to try to power through with stimulants alone.

questions.q: Being caught driving under the influence of alcohol in the UAE typically results in:
options: A small fine only
Arrest, heavy fine, possible imprisonment, and licence suspension
A warning for first-time offenders
No consequence if no accident occurred
questions.explanation: Driving under the influence is treated as a serious criminal offence in the UAE with severe legal consequences.

questions.q: According to the RTA handbook's 2010 crash data, what proportion of crashes in Dubai were caused by drivers under the influence of alcohol?
questions.explanation: Verified in the RTA handbook: it states that 14.33% of crashes in Dubai are caused by drivers who were under the influence of alcohol.

questions.q: Alcohol and drugs make driving dangerous mainly because they:
options: Improve your reaction time
Make it harder to judge risks, distance and speed, and give a false sense of confidence
Only affect your sense of smell
Have no effect on judgement, only on movement
questions.explanation: Verified in the RTA handbook: alcohol and drugs make it more difficult to judge risks including distance and speed, and give a false sense of confidence that can encourage risk-taking.

questions.q: If you have been drinking, the safest plan before driving is to:
options: Drink coffee and wait 10 minutes
Open the windows and drive slowly
Arrange to be picked up by someone alcohol-free, or take a taxi
Drive only on familiar roads
questions.explanation: Verified in the RTA handbook: to stay safe, plan ahead and arrange to be picked up by someone who is alcohol or drug free, or take a taxi.

questions.q: Rumble strips on the road are especially helpful for drivers who are:
options: Speeding
Tired or drowsy on a long drive
Reversing
Towing a trailer
questions.explanation: Verified in the RTA handbook: rumble strips warn drivers approaching a hazard, and this vibration and sound is especially helpful for drivers on a long drive who may be feeling tired or sleepy.

questions.q: Under UAE Federal Traffic Law (Article 10.7), you must not drive your vehicle when:
options: Tired, as you may become unable to control your car
The fuel tank is below half full
You are wearing sunglasses
You have passengers under 18
questions.explanation: Article 10.7 of UAE Federal Traffic Law No. 21 of 1995 states you must not drive when tired, as you may become unable to control your car (RTA Light Motor Vehicle Handbook).

questions.q: Which of the following is a warning sign that you should stop driving and rest?
options: Constant yawning and starting to drift across your lane
Feeling fully alert and focused on the road
Driving exactly at the posted speed limit
Checking your mirrors regularly
questions.explanation: The RTA Light Motor Vehicle Handbook lists constant yawning, drifting across the lane, fuzzy eyesight, and not remembering the last few kilometres driven as signs that it is time to stop and rest.

questions.q: The RTA Light Motor Vehicle Handbook notes that in one month in Dubai, how many people died due to careless and sleepy driving?
questions.explanation: The handbook states: “In one month in Dubai alone, 13 people died due to careless and sleepy drivers,” used to underline the danger of driving while tired.

questions.q: Driving while extremely fatigued mainly affects a driver because it:
options: Has no measurable effect on driving ability
Slows reaction time and impairs judgement, in a similar way to being under the influence of alcohol
Only affects a driver's comfort, not their ability to control the vehicle
Improves concentration by keeping the driver alert to discomfort
questions.explanation: Severe fatigue slows reaction time and impairs judgement and attention in ways that resemble alcohol impairment, even though no alcohol is involved — which is why "drowsy driving" is treated as seriously as drink-driving in road safety guidance.

questions.q: Signs that a nearby driver may be dangerously fatigued or impaired include weaving within the lane, drifting onto road markings, and delayed reactions to traffic changes. If you notice this, you should:
options: Follow closely so you can react to whatever they do next
Overtake immediately regardless of conditions, to get away from them fast
Keep a generous distance, avoid overtaking alongside them, and if possible let them pass or move well away
Flash your headlights repeatedly to alert them
questions.explanation: A vehicle weaving or reacting slowly may be driven by someone fatigued, impaired, or distracted and could behave unpredictably. Keeping extra distance and avoiding being alongside them reduces your risk if they make a sudden or dangerous move.

questions.q: A 'microsleep' while driving refers to:
options: A brief nap taken safely at a rest stop
A few seconds of involuntary sleep with the eyes open or closed, occurring while still driving -- extremely dangerous since the vehicle continues uncontrolled
A short break recommended every two hours
A state of light distraction, such as glancing at the radio
questions.explanation: A microsleep is an involuntary lapse into sleep lasting a few seconds that a fatigued person may not even notice happened, but during which a moving vehicle receives no steering or braking input -- a major cause of fatigue-related crashes.

questions.q: Before going out somewhere you plan to drink alcohol, the safest plan is to:
options: Arrange a designated (non-drinking) driver, a taxi, or ride-hailing service in advance
Decide later, once at the venue, whether you feel able to drive
Drink only a small amount so you can still drive carefully
Plan to sleep in the car for an hour before driving
questions.explanation: Deciding on a safe way home before drinking removes the need to judge your own impairment later, which alcohol itself makes unreliable. Arranging a designated driver, taxi, or ride-hailing service in advance is the most reliable plan.

questions.q: Combining alcohol with fatigue (tiredness) while driving is especially dangerous because:
options: Their effects on reaction time and judgement compound each other, making the combined impairment worse than either alone
Fatigue cancels out the effects of alcohol
Only one of the two actually affects driving ability
Alcohol only affects vision, and fatigue only affects hearing
questions.explanation: Alcohol and fatigue each independently slow reaction time and impair judgement; together their effects add up, making a driver far more dangerous than either factor alone.

questions.q: Some medications carry a warning that they may cause drowsiness or slower reactions. A driver taking such medication should:
options: Ignore the warning since medication is always safe to drive on
Only worry about it if driving at night
Check the label carefully and avoid driving if warned, since the effect can resemble alcohol impairment
Take a double dose to counteract the drowsiness
questions.explanation: Medications that cause drowsiness or slowed reactions can impair driving ability similarly to alcohol, so drivers should follow label warnings and avoid driving if warned.

questions.q: After a poor night's sleep, a driver's performance the next day can be:
options: Completely unaffected as long as no alcohol was consumed
Significantly impaired, with slower reaction time and reduced concentration, even without drinking any alcohol
Only affected in the evening, never in the morning
Improved due to extra alertness from tiredness
questions.explanation: Sleep deprivation impairs reaction time, concentration, and judgement in ways that can be as serious as alcohol impairment, regardless of whether any alcohol was consumed.

questions.q: Drinking caffeine or an energy drink is not a real solution for driver fatigue mainly because:
options: Caffeine has no effect on alertness at all
It is illegal to drink caffeine while driving
It permanently removes the need for sleep
It only provides temporary alertness while the underlying tiredness and its effects on reaction time remain, and the effect wears off
questions.explanation: Caffeine can temporarily mask feelings of sleepiness, but it does not reverse the underlying impairment to reaction time and judgement, and its effect fades, sometimes leaving a driver suddenly worse off.

questions.q: You start yawning repeatedly and drifting slightly within your lane on a long drive. What is the safest response?
options: Turn up the music and keep driving
Open the window and push on to your destination
Stop at the next safe place and rest before continuing
Drive faster to finish the trip sooner
questions.explanation: Yawning and lane drift are early fatigue warning signs; the only reliably safe response is to stop and rest, not to try to power through with music, air, or speed.

questions.q: Which of the following can impair driving ability similarly to alcohol, even though it is legal?
options: Drinking water
Severe sleep deprivation
Wearing sunglasses at night
Using air conditioning
questions.explanation: Severe fatigue/sleep deprivation slows reaction time and judgment in ways comparable to alcohol impairment, even though it is not illegal on its own.

questions.q: Black points on a UAE driving licence are used to:
options: Give discounts on registration
Track serious or repeated traffic violations and can lead to licence suspension
Reward safe drivers
Track fuel consumption
questions.explanation: Black points accumulate for serious violations; reaching certain thresholds can suspend or revoke the driving licence.

questions.q: If a driver accumulates 24 black points within one year, the usual consequence is:
options: A written warning only, with no other action
Licence confiscation for 3 months the first time, escalating to 6 then 12 months (plus a mandatory course) for repeat occurrences
An automatic fine only, with no action against the licence
Permanent, non-appealable licence cancellation on the first occurrence
questions.explanation: Per the RTA Light Motor Vehicle Handbook, reaching 24 black points in a year leads to licence confiscation for three months the first time, six months if it happens again within a year, and twelve months (plus passing a special course) the third time.

questions.q: Jumping a red traffic light in the UAE typically results in:
options: A verbal warning only
A fine of AED 800 and 8 black points
No fine, but 24 black points
A fine only, with no black points added
questions.explanation: The RTA Light Motor Vehicle Handbook's violations table lists jumping a red light as an AED 800 fine carrying 8 black points.

questions.q: Unpaid traffic fines in the UAE can result in:
options: No consequence beyond the amount owed
Vehicle registration renewal being blocked until fines are paid
Automatic cancellation of the fine after a year
A reduction in the fine amount over time
questions.explanation: Outstanding fines must generally be cleared before vehicle registration (Mulkiya) can be renewed.

questions.q: Driving without a valid licence in the UAE is:
options: A minor issue with no fine
A serious offence with a heavy fine and possible vehicle impoundment
Allowed for UAE residents only
Only an issue for tourists
questions.explanation: Driving without a valid licence is a serious offence, carrying a substantial fine and the vehicle may be impounded.

questions.q: Black points on a licence usually expire or are cleared:
options: Never
After a period of time set by the RTA if no further violations occur
Immediately after payment of the fine
Only when the licence is renewed
questions.explanation: Black points typically clear after a defined period without further violations, according to RTA rules.

questions.q: If a driver accumulates 24 black points within one year for the first time, the licence is:
options: Cancelled permanently
Confiscated for 3 months
Confiscated for 6 months
Confiscated for 12 months, with a mandatory course required
questions.explanation: Verified in the RTA handbook: reaching 24 points in a year leads to a 3-month licence confiscation the first time, 6 months the second time it happens again within a year, and 12 months plus a mandatory special course the third time.

questions.q: Driving in a dedicated bus or taxi lane in Dubai without authorisation carries a fine of:
options: AED 200
AED 400
AED 600
questions.explanation: Verified in the RTA handbook: any driver caught illegally using a bus or taxi lane will be fined AED 600.

questions.q: Passing a Salik toll point without a valid tag fitted to the vehicle results in a fine that:
options: Stays fixed at AED 50 no matter how many times it happens
Escalates: AED 100 for the first trip, AED 200 for the second, AED 400 for the third and every trip after that
Is only a warning, with no fine for the first three times
Is capped at AED 24, the same as the daily toll maximum
questions.explanation: Verified in the RTA handbook's Salik violations table: passing without a tag is fined AED 100 (first trip), AED 200 (second trip), and AED 400 (third and subsequent trips).

questions.q: Dubai's public parking is divided into Code A and Code B zones. What is the key difference?
options: Code A allows free parking, Code B does not
Code A is short-stay (max 4 hours), Code B is long-stay (max 24 hours)
Code A is for motorcycles only
Code B is only for government vehicles
questions.explanation: RTA divides paid parking into Code A (side-road parking, short stay up to 4 hours) and Code B (dedicated parking yards, long stay up to 24 hours), each with its own tariff.

questions.q: What is the standard hourly tariff at a Multi-Storey Car Parking (MSCP) facility in Dubai, which operates 24/7?
options: AED 1.00/hour
AED 3.00/hour
AED 10.00/hour
It is always free after 6pm
questions.explanation: RTA Multi-Storey Car Parking facilities operate 24 hours a day at a standard tariff of AED 3.00 per hour.

questions.q: Roughly how much can a driver be fined per calendar year for repeated Salik toll violations (no tag/insufficient balance), per the RTA handbook?
options: There is no annual cap
Up to AED 1,000 per year
Up to AED 10,000 per year maximum violation amount
Violations are forgiven after 3 months
questions.explanation: The handbook sets a maximum Salik violation amount of AED 10,000 per calendar year, though escalating per-trip fines (AED 100/200/400) apply before that cap.

questions.q: 'Lane discipline' on a highway mainly means:
options: Staying in one lane and only changing when necessary and safe, using signals
Switching lanes frequently to move faster
Always driving in the leftmost lane
Driving on the hard shoulder when busy
questions.explanation: Good lane discipline means committing to a lane, signalling clearly, and changing only when necessary and safe.

questions.q: The hard shoulder on a highway should be used for:
options: Overtaking during heavy traffic
Emergency stops only
A regular driving lane during rush hour
Parking to make a phone call
questions.explanation: The hard shoulder is reserved strictly for emergencies, breakdowns, or use by emergency vehicles.

questions.q: When merging onto a highway from an on-ramp, a driver should:
options: Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a full gap
Match the highway's traffic speed and merge smoothly when safe
Force other vehicles to slow down
Merge only from the leftmost lane
questions.explanation: Merging drivers should accelerate to match traffic speed and merge into a safe gap smoothly, without stopping unnecessarily.

questions.q: Undertaking (overtaking from the right/inside lane) in the UAE is:
options: Always allowed on highways
Generally discouraged or prohibited and considered dangerous
Required when the left lane is occupied
Only for motorcycles
questions.explanation: Undertaking is dangerous and against safe driving practice, since drivers do not expect to be passed from the inside.

questions.q: A minimum safe following distance in good conditions is often measured using:
options: The 2-second rule (or more in poor conditions)
A fixed distance of 1 metre
No specific method is used
The width of the vehicle only
questions.explanation: The 2-second rule (increased in rain, fog, or at higher speeds) helps drivers keep a safe following distance.

questions.q: Sudden or unnecessary braking on a highway is dangerous because:
options: It saves fuel for the driver behind
It can cause multi-vehicle collisions from following traffic
It is required by law every few kilometres
It has no real risk on modern highways
questions.explanation: Sudden braking without cause can trigger chain-reaction collisions, especially at highway speeds.

questions.q: When overtaking another vehicle travelling in the same direction, you must pass on:
options: Either side, whichever is clearer
The left only
The right only
The hard shoulder
questions.explanation: Verified in the RTA handbook (Article 10.5): a driver must only pass other vehicles travelling in the same direction on the left.

questions.q: If another vehicle is overtaking you, the correct response is to:
options: Speed up so it cannot pass
Slow down and keep to the right
Move to the left lane immediately
Flash your headlights and hold your lane
questions.explanation: Verified in the RTA handbook (Article 54): if someone is overtaking you, you must slow down and keep to the right.

questions.q: According to the RTA handbook, you must NOT overtake at:
options: A straight, clear stretch of road
Intersections and roundabouts
A dual carriageway with a broken centre line
A designated overtaking lane
questions.explanation: Verified in the RTA handbook: overtaking is prohibited where the road is not clearly visible, when oncoming traffic doesn't allow it safely, and specifically at intersections and roundabouts.

questions.q: Before pulling out to overtake a vehicle on a two-way road, the handbook advises staying at least how far behind it?
options: Half a second
Two seconds
Ten seconds
One car length only
questions.explanation: Verified in the RTA handbook: you should be at least two seconds behind the vehicle you are about to overtake, giving better vision and room to build up speed.

questions.q: According to the RTA handbook, overtaking a large truck on the open road typically takes about:
options: 5 seconds
25 seconds
60 seconds
2 minutes
questions.explanation: Verified in the RTA handbook: it takes about 25 seconds to overtake a large truck on the open road, which is a long time to spend on the wrong side of the road.

questions.q: You must not cross which type of line to overtake another vehicle?
options: A single broken white line
A single solid white/yellow line dividing traffic
Lane arrows painted on the road
A pedestrian crossing's zebra markings
questions.explanation: Verified in the RTA handbook (Article 58): you must not cross a single solid line on the road which divides traffic, whether to overtake or to turn, except in an emergency.

questions.q: A vehicle's total stopping distance is the reaction distance (before the brakes are applied) plus the braking distance. As speed increases, this total stopping distance:
options: Stays roughly the same regardless of speed
Increases, and increases more sharply than speed itself (not just in direct proportion)
Decreases, because faster vehicles have better brakes
Only increases on wet roads
questions.explanation: Reaction distance increases in direct proportion to speed, but braking distance increases with the square of speed — so doubling your speed more than doubles your overall stopping distance, which is why speeding is especially dangerous.

questions.q: On a wet road, if your vehicle begins to 'hydroplane' (skate on a film of water, losing grip), you should:
options: Brake hard immediately to slow down
Ease off the accelerator gently, avoid braking or steering sharply, and let the vehicle slow until the tyres regain grip
Steer hard in the opposite direction of the skid
Accelerate to drive through the water faster
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when a layer of water lifts the tyres off the road surface. Sudden braking or steering can make the vehicle spin; easing off the accelerator lets the vehicle slow down gradually until the tyres reconnect with the road.

questions.q: When driving directly into strong sun glare (for example at sunrise or sunset), a driver should:
options: Stare directly at the road ahead to stay oriented
Follow the vehicle ahead as closely as possible so you can see its brake lights
Use the sun visor or sunglasses, slow down, and increase the following distance since glare can hide hazards
Turn on high-beam headlights to compensate
questions.explanation: Strong glare can briefly blind a driver to hazards such as a stopped vehicle or a pedestrian. Using a visor/sunglasses, slowing down, and leaving extra following distance give more time to react safely.

questions.q: Compared to daytime, driving at night requires:
options: The same following distance, since speed limits do not change
A shorter following distance, since roads are usually quieter
No change in driving technique
A greater following distance, since headlights illuminate less distance than daylight allows a driver to see
questions.explanation: Headlights typically illuminate far less distance than a driver can see clearly in daylight, so hazards are spotted later at night. Increasing the following distance gives more time to react safely.

questions.q: If a sudden sandstorm severely reduces visibility while you are driving on a highway, you should:
options: Keep your normal speed but turn on hazard lights
Reduce speed significantly, turn on low-beam headlights, and if visibility becomes extremely poor, safely move off the road (not stop in a live lane)
Accelerate to drive out of the sandstorm quickly
Stop immediately in your current lane
questions.explanation: Sudden sandstorms are a real UAE highway hazard. Drivers should slow down well below the posted limit, use low beams (not high beams, which reflect off dust), and if visibility drops close to zero, exit the road safely rather than stopping in a live lane where following vehicles could collide with them.

questions.q: If a front tyre suddenly bursts (a blowout) while driving at speed, the correct response is to:
options: Ease off the accelerator gradually, hold the steering wheel firmly and steady, and let the vehicle slow down before braking gently
Brake hard immediately to stop as fast as possible
Steer sharply to correct the pull and swerve into another lane
Accelerate briefly to maintain control
questions.explanation: A sudden tyre blowout can pull the vehicle toward the burst tyre. Braking hard or steering sharply can cause loss of control; easing off the accelerator and holding the wheel steady lets the vehicle slow naturally before gentle, gradual braking once it is stable.

questions.q: On a wet road, the safe following distance compared to dry conditions should be:
options: Exactly the same, since speed limits are unchanged
Slightly shorter, since wet roads encourage slower speeds anyway
At least doubled, since braking distances increase significantly on a wet surface
Irrelevant, since anti-lock brakes remove all extra stopping distance
questions.explanation: Wet roads reduce tyre grip and significantly increase braking distance. Doubling the normal following distance (or more) gives a driver enough space and time to stop safely if the vehicle ahead brakes.

questions.q: When you see a vehicle signalling to merge into your lane from an on-ramp, and it is safe to do so, you should:
options: Speed up to close the gap so the vehicle cannot merge
Ease off slightly or adjust position, if it is safe, to make room for the merging vehicle
Ignore it, since the merging driver is fully responsible for finding a gap
Flash your headlights repeatedly to warn it away
questions.explanation: Smooth highway merging works best as a shared responsibility: while the merging driver must find a safe gap, drivers already on the highway can help by easing off slightly or moving over (when safe) to make space, reducing sudden braking and collision risk.

questions.q: Before changing lanes on a highway, checking mirrors is not enough on its own because:
options: Mirrors show more than a driver needs to see
A vehicle can be in a 'blind spot' that mirrors don't cover, so a shoulder check (a quick glance over the shoulder) is also needed
Mirrors are only useful at low speed
Checking mirrors takes too much time
questions.explanation: Every vehicle has blind spots that side and rear-view mirrors don't fully cover, so a driver must also glance over the shoulder before changing lanes.

questions.q: Lingering in the blind spot beside or slightly behind a large truck or bus is dangerous mainly because:
options: The truck or bus driver may not be able to see your vehicle at all in that position
It is illegal to drive next to a truck
It saves fuel to stay close to a large vehicle
Trucks always drive faster than cars
questions.explanation: Large vehicles have much bigger blind spots than cars; a vehicle sitting in that zone may be completely invisible to the truck or bus driver.

questions.q: If you are following a large vehicle and cannot see the road ahead of it in your line of sight, you should:
options: Move as close as possible to see under the vehicle
Overtake immediately regardless of visibility
Drop back further until you have a clearer view of the road ahead, or wait for a safe, clear opportunity to overtake
Flash your headlights until the vehicle moves aside
questions.explanation: Reducing following distance to a large vehicle you can't see past only reduces your own reaction time; it's safer to drop back for a better view or wait for a safe overtaking gap.

questions.q: Approaching a highway construction zone where lanes are narrowed and workers are present, a driver should:
options: Maintain normal highway speed since it is still a highway
Overtake other vehicles to get through the zone quickly
Ignore temporary signs since they are not permanent
Reduce speed well in advance and follow the temporary lane markings and signs
questions.explanation: Construction zones bring narrower lanes, workers close to traffic, and changed layouts, so speed must be reduced early and temporary signs followed carefully.

questions.q: Slowing down to look at a crash or incident on the opposite side of the highway ('rubbernecking') is a hazard mainly because it:
options: Helps other drivers understand what happened
Causes unnecessary slowdowns and distraction in your own lane, which can lead to a rear-end collision or a second crash
Is required by traffic law
Has no real effect on traffic flow
questions.explanation: Rubbernecking distracts the driver from the road ahead and creates sudden, unnecessary braking in lanes unaffected by the original incident, which is a common cause of secondary crashes.

questions.q: What does a solid white line between lanes (as opposed to a dashed line) generally indicate?
options: Lane changing is encouraged here
Lane changing should be avoided/is prohibited here
It has no meaning
It only applies to trucks
questions.explanation: A solid lane line indicates that changing lanes at that point should be avoided or is prohibited, unlike a dashed line which permits lane changes when safe.

questions.q: For heavy vehicle and bus drivers, the best time to take a rest break is:
options: Before you become tired
As soon as you become tired
Only once you reach your final destination
Only during specific RTA-designated hours
questions.explanation: Planning rest breaks before fatigue sets in, rather than waiting until you already feel tired, is the recommended approach in heavy-vehicle driver training.

questions.q: Which of the following is most likely to cause drowsiness while driving a heavy vehicle?
options: Taking cold and allergy tablets
Suffering from mild hay fever
Taking a short nap before starting to drive
Opening a window for fresh air
questions.explanation: Many cold and allergy (antihistamine) medications cause drowsiness as a side effect, which is a serious risk for a driver; a short nap before driving actually helps alertness.

questions.q: Which food choice is best for a heavy vehicle driver during a long trip?
options: A heavy, fried meal
A bag of fresh fruit
A large bowl of pasta
Sugary snacks and energy drinks only
questions.explanation: Light, fresh food such as fruit is easier to digest and less likely to cause the sluggishness that heavy or sugary meals can bring on during a long drive.

questions.q: The best way to help prevent fatigue on a long-distance trip is to travel during:
options: The hours you are normally awake
Daylight hours only, regardless of your normal sleep pattern
Night hours only, to avoid traffic
It makes no difference when you travel
questions.explanation: Driving during your normal waking hours works with your body clock, while driving through your usual sleep hours increases the risk of fatigue regardless of whether it is day or night.

questions.q: During a rest stop on a long trip, light exercise such as stretching or touching your toes:
options: Can help keep you alert
Has no effect on alertness
Should never be done before a long trip
Increases fatigue
questions.explanation: Light physical activity during a break helps circulation and alertness, making it a useful part of managing fatigue on long trips.

questions.q: Rocks or mud caught in the space between a heavy vehicle's dual (twin) wheels may cause:
options: A tyre to lose pressure
The engine to overheat
The gearbox to slip
No effect on the tyres at all
questions.explanation: The Truck and Bus Handbook's pre-trip inspection checklist states: rocks or mud caught between dual wheels can unbalance a wheel and damage the tyre side walls and wheel bearings — which is why drivers must check the spacing between dual wheels.

questions.q: Under RTA rules, a heavy vehicle failing to keep proper lane discipline (using lanes not permitted for heavy vehicles) is a violation that carries:
options: A fine of AED 600 and 6 black points
A fine of AED 5000 and no black points
No fine, only a verbal warning
Automatic and immediate licence cancellation
questions.explanation: The RTA Light Motor Vehicle Handbook's violations table lists heavy-vehicle lane discipline breaches with a fine of AED 600 and 6 black points.

questions.q: Overloading a heavy vehicle, or having its load protrude without permission, is a violation that carries:
options: A fine of AED 500 and 6 black points
No fine, only vehicle impoundment
A fine of AED 5000 and 12 black points
A warning only, for the first offence
questions.explanation: The RTA handbook's violations table lists overloading or an unauthorised protruding load from a heavy vehicle with a fine of AED 500 and 6 black points.

questions.q: A load that falls or leaks from a heavy vehicle onto the road is a violation that carries:
options: A fine of AED 3000 and 21 black points
A fine of AED 100 and no black points
No fine if the load is retrieved quickly
A fine, but no black points at all
questions.explanation: The RTA handbook's violations table lists a falling or leaking load with a fine of AED 3000 and 21 black points -- one of the more serious violations short of court-decided offences.

questions.q: Dangerous overtaking by a truck is a violation under RTA rules that carries:
options: A fine of AED 800 and 24 black points
A fine of AED 200 and 2 black points
No black points, a fine only
A warning only, no fine
questions.explanation: The RTA handbook's violations table lists dangerous overtaking by trucks with a fine of AED 800 and 24 black points -- the same severe points tier as driving without number plates.

questions.q: Failing to cover the load of a truck (for example, loose gravel or sand) in the UAE carries:
options: A fine of AED 3000
No fine, a verbal warning only
A fine of AED 50
Suspension of the vehicle's registration only, with no fine
questions.explanation: The RTA handbook's violations table lists not covering a truck's load with a fine of AED 3000.

questions.q: According to the RTA's Truck and Bus Handbook, a heavy vehicle or bus driver should never drive for more than how many hours within any 24-hour period?
options: 6 hours
8 hours
10 hours
12 hours
questions.explanation: Verified in the RTA Truck and Bus Handbook (Part 2, 'Take Breaks'): drivers should take short breaks before becoming tired and should never drive for more than 10 hours in any 24-hour period.

questions.q: On a UAE freeway, overtaking another vehicle by using the hard shoulder is:
options: Allowed if your vehicle is a truck
Allowed only during heavy congestion
Not allowed under any circumstance
Allowed if you signal clearly first
questions.explanation: Verified in the RTA handbook: drivers must not overtake on the hard shoulder of the road; it is reserved for emergencies and breakdowns, not for bypassing traffic.

questions.q: A heavy vehicle that causes a falling or leaking load on the road is penalised with:
options: 6 black points
12 black points
21 black points
24 black points
questions.explanation: Verified in the RTA handbook's violations table: a falling or leaking load carries 21 black points, reflecting the serious hazard it creates for following traffic.

questions.q: After you press the brake pedal on a heavy vehicle with air brakes, there is a delay before the brakes fully act. About how long is this delay?
options: No delay at all
Up to about one second
About 10 seconds
About one minute
questions.explanation: Air takes time to travel through the system after the pedal is pressed — up to about a one-second delay — so heavy-vehicle drivers must start braking earlier than in a light vehicle (Truck and Bus Handbook).

questions.q: On a long downhill, continuous heavy braking causes “brake fade” because:
options: The brake linings overheat and gradually lose their stopping power
The brake pedal physically locks in place
The tyres automatically deflate
The engine shuts off to protect itself
questions.explanation: Continuous heavy braking on a long hill heats up the brake linings until they no longer slow the vehicle effectively — this is called brake fade (Truck and Bus Handbook).

questions.q: To help prevent brake fade before starting down a long hill in a heavy vehicle, you should:
options: Shift into a lower gear before you start going down
Shift into neutral and coast down
Turn off the engine to save fuel
Apply the handbrake fully for the whole descent
questions.explanation: Shifting into a lower gear before a long descent lets engine braking help slow the vehicle, so the brakes are used less and are less likely to overheat and fade (Truck and Bus Handbook).

questions.q: Because a heavy vehicle takes longer to slow down and stop, a driver should look ahead on the road for about how many seconds' worth of travel?
options: 2-3 seconds
12-15 seconds
30-40 seconds
Less than 1 second
questions.explanation: Heavy-vehicle drivers need to know what is on the road 12 to 15 seconds ahead, since large vehicles take longer to slow down, change lanes, or stop (Truck and Bus Handbook).

questions.q: When a long heavy vehicle goes around a turn, the rear wheels usually follow a shorter, tighter path than the front wheels. This is called:
options: Cut-in
Aquaplaning
Brake fade
Double-clutching
questions.explanation: This effect is called “cut-in”; the sharper the turn and the longer the vehicle, the greater the cut-in, so drivers must position their approach accordingly (Truck and Bus Handbook).

questions.q: When reversing an articulated (trailer) heavy vehicle, the trailer:
options: Moves in exactly the same direction the steering wheel is turned
Moves contrary to (opposite of) the direction the steering wheel is turned
Cannot move at all while reversing
Straightens itself automatically without steering input
questions.explanation: The trailer moves contrary to the direction of the steering when reversing, so drivers need special technique and practice, using all mirrors and correcting drift immediately (Truck and Bus Handbook).

questions.q: Before descending a long, steep gradient in a heavy vehicle, a driver should:
options: Select a lower gear before starting the descent, using engine braking to help control speed rather than relying only on the brakes
Select the highest gear to minimise engine noise
Turn off the engine to save fuel while coasting down
Apply the brakes continuously and firmly the whole way down
questions.explanation: Riding the brakes continuously on a long descent can cause them to overheat and fade (lose stopping power). Selecting a lower gear before the descent uses engine braking to help control speed, keeping the brakes available and effective for the whole descent.

questions.q: 'Brake fade' in a heavy vehicle refers to:
options: A brake light that flickers due to a wiring fault
The natural wear of brake pads over the vehicle's lifetime
A temporary loss of braking power, usually from overheated brakes after prolonged or heavy use (such as continuous braking down a long hill)
A legal requirement to service brakes every year
questions.explanation: Brake fade happens when brakes overheat from prolonged or heavy use and temporarily lose stopping power. It is a serious risk for heavy vehicles on long descents, which is why engine braking and a lower gear are used to reduce reliance on the brakes.

questions.q: Because heavy vehicles and buses have much larger blind spots than cars, other drivers should mainly:
options: Drive as close as possible behind them to save fuel
Avoid lingering directly beside or close behind a heavy vehicle where its driver may not be able to see them
Overtake them only on the right side, never the left
Assume the heavy vehicle driver always sees them
questions.explanation: A car sitting in a heavy vehicle's large blind spot may be completely invisible to its driver, so it is safer to pass through such zones quickly rather than linger in them.

questions.q: When a heavy vehicle or bus makes a wide turn, other drivers should:
options: Try to squeeze into the gap it leaves on the inside of the turn
Overtake it during the turn to save time
Not attempt to fill the space it leaves during the turn, since the heavy vehicle needs that space to complete it safely
Sound the horn to make it turn faster
questions.explanation: A heavy vehicle swings wide to complete a turn safely because of its length; a car squeezing into the gap it leaves risks being struck as the vehicle completes the turn.

questions.q: A heavy vehicle's load must be properly secured mainly because an unsecured load can:
options: Shift during braking or turning, affecting the vehicle's balance and braking, or fall onto the road and endanger other traffic
Only affect the vehicle's fuel economy
Improve the vehicle's stability if left loose
Only matter for appearance, not safety
questions.explanation: A shifting or falling load can seriously destabilize a heavy vehicle and create a direct hazard for following or nearby traffic, which is why load security rules are strictly enforced.

questions.q: Because heavy vehicles accelerate much more slowly than cars, a driver merging in front of one should:
options: Merge as close as possible since heavy vehicles can always stop quickly
Allow extra space when merging in front of a heavy vehicle, since it needs more distance and time to slow down or adjust
Ignore the heavy vehicle's size since all vehicles must yield equally
Expect the heavy vehicle to speed up and create space
questions.explanation: A heavy vehicle needs significantly more distance and time to slow down or adjust speed than a car, so a driver merging in front of one should leave extra space rather than cutting in closely.

questions.q: If you are fatigued while riding a motorcycle, you will:
options: Not be able to make decisions quickly
Be able to make decisions just as quickly as normal
Notice no difference in your riding
Ride more cautiously without even trying
questions.explanation: Fatigue slows reaction time and judgement, making it harder to make quick, safe decisions while riding.

questions.q: When checking a motorcycle's rear brake, it should be adjusted so that it:
options: Stops the motorcycle when only lightly applied
Stops the motorcycle when fully applied
Never fully stops the motorcycle
Locks immediately at any pressure
questions.explanation: A correctly adjusted rear brake should bring the motorcycle to a stop when fully applied, without locking at the slightest touch.

questions.q: When checking a motorcycle's front brake, it should be adjusted so that it:
options: Stops the motorcycle when only lightly applied
Stops the motorcycle when fully applied
Does not stop the motorcycle even when fully applied
Only works when the engine is off
questions.explanation: Like the rear brake, a correctly adjusted front brake should stop the motorcycle when fully applied.

questions.q: What should each mirror fitted to a motorcycle let the rider see?
options: Mainly the traffic directly behind
Only the lane next to the rider
As much as possible of the lane next to the rider and of the traffic behind
Nothing in front of the rider
questions.explanation: Motorcycle mirrors should be adjusted to show as much as possible of the adjacent lane and the traffic behind, to cover blind spots.

questions.q: Why is it dangerous to use a second-hand (used) motorcycle helmet?
options: It may have damage that is not visible from the outside
It may simply be an outdated design
It is not considered socially acceptable
It is always the wrong size
questions.explanation: A used helmet may have suffered an impact that weakened its protective foam without leaving visible external damage, so its crash protection can no longer be trusted.

questions.q: When fully applied, which brakes should be able to hold a stationary motorcycle?
options: The front brake only
The rear brake only
Both the front and rear brakes
Neither brake; only the side stand holds the bike
questions.explanation: Both the front and rear brakes, when fully applied and in good working order, should each be capable of holding the motorcycle stationary.

questions.q: When a motorcycle's throttle is opened wide and then released, it should:
options: Snap shut
Gradually close over several seconds
Remain in place until manually closed
Continue accelerating briefly
questions.explanation: A healthy throttle return spring should snap the throttle fully shut as soon as it is released, which is an important pre-ride safety check.

questions.q: A motorcycle's drive chain should:
options: Have no slack at all
Be lubricated and have its tension adjusted correctly
Always have 10-20 mm of slack no matter what the manual says
Never be checked once it is fitted
questions.explanation: The chain should be kept lubricated with its tension set to the manufacturer's specification; too tight or too loose can cause premature wear or a dangerous failure.

questions.q: When riding through a corner, a motorcycle rider should:
options: Stay right of centre in the lane to keep away from oncoming vehicles
Stay left of centre in the lane to be more easily seen
Position on the road so they can see through the corner and be seen by other drivers
Always ride in the exact centre of the lane regardless of visibility
questions.explanation: Good cornering technique means positioning yourself in the lane for the best view through the bend and the best visibility to other road users, adjusting position as the corner requires.

questions.q: Under UAE traffic law, wearing an approved helmet on a motorcycle is required for:
options: The rider only
The rider and any pillion (passenger)
Only riders under 18 years old
Only when riding on highways, not urban roads
questions.explanation: Confirmed in the RTA-affiliated Drive Dubai motorcycle theory-test training deck: when riding with a pillion passenger, an approved helmet is required for both the rider and the pillion passenger, not the rider alone.

questions.q: Lane splitting (riding a motorcycle between lanes of stationary or slow-moving traffic) in the UAE is:
options: Legal at any speed difference between the motorcycle and the traffic
Generally not permitted; motorcycles must keep to a marked lane like other vehicles
Only illegal on Sheikh Zayed Road
Actively encouraged by the RTA to reduce congestion
questions.explanation: UAE practice generally treats lane splitting as not permitted, with motorcycles expected to stay within a marked lane, but this pass could not confirm the exact statutory article, so it remains flagged for verification against the current traffic law text.

questions.q: When carrying a pillion passenger on a motorcycle in the UAE, the rider must ensure:
options: No more than one pillion passenger, seated on a proper seat with footrests and wearing a helmet
Up to two pillion passengers are allowed if the motorcycle is large enough
The pillion passenger does not need a helmet if the trip is short
There is no restriction on the number of passengers carried
questions.explanation: Standard motorcycle safety practice limits a motorcycle to one pillion passenger, properly seated and helmeted; the exact UAE statutory limit was not directly confirmed in the sources used for this pass, so it remains flagged.

questions.q: When overtaking a cyclist or motorcyclist, a driver should:
options: Pass as close as possible to save road space
Only move left if an entire lane is completely free first
Move safely to the left, leaving at least one metre of clearance
Sound the horn continuously while passing
questions.explanation: Verified in the RTA handbook: drivers should only overtake a cyclist or motorcyclist if they can safely move left, leaving at least one metre of clearance, especially useful near parked cars where a door could open unexpectedly.

questions.q: Motorcyclists and cyclists in the UAE are permitted to:
options: Use only the far-left edge of their lane at all times
Use the full width of their traffic lane
Ride two-abreast in the same lane as cars, without restriction
Use the hard shoulder as a dedicated riding lane
questions.explanation: Verified in the RTA handbook: motorcyclists and cyclists are permitted to use the full width of the road lane, so other drivers must leave them enough space to do so safely.

questions.q: A motorcyclist should always buy a new helmet rather than a second-hand one mainly because a second-hand helmet:
options: Is always the wrong size
May have hidden damage that is not visible but weakens its protection
Is always an outdated design
Costs more to maintain
questions.explanation: This is standard motorcycle-safety guidance (also used in UAE motorcycle rider training materials): a second-hand helmet may have sustained impact damage that isn't visible but that seriously reduces its ability to protect in a crash.

questions.q: A motorcyclist's protective gear should generally include:
options: A helmet only; other gear is unnecessary
A full set of protective gear — helmet, jacket, gloves, and suitable footwear — since a crash can injure any part of the body
Sunglasses only, for glare protection
Gear is only needed for long trips, not short ones
questions.explanation: A motorcyclist has far less physical protection than a car occupant, so a full set of protective gear (helmet, jacket, gloves, sturdy footwear) — not just a helmet — reduces the risk of injury to the whole body in a fall or crash.

questions.q: On a wet road, a motorcycle rider should:
options: Ride at the same speed as usual, since motorcycle tyres grip better than car tyres
Slow down, avoid sudden braking or sharp turns, and be especially cautious over painted road markings and metal surfaces, which become slicker when wet
Only worry about wet roads on a highway, not in the city
Increase speed slightly to pass through wet patches faster
questions.explanation: A motorcycle has far less contact area with the road than a car, so it loses grip more easily on wet surfaces -- especially over painted lane markings, manhole covers, and metal grates, which become noticeably more slippery when wet.

questions.q: Compared to a car, a motorcycle generally needs a following distance that is:
options: Shorter, since motorcycles are more agile
The same, since the rules are identical for all vehicles
Irrelevant, since motorcycles can always swerve to avoid a collision
At least as long, and often longer, since a motorcycle is less stable, has less protection in a collision, and can be harder for the rider ahead to see clearly in a mirror
questions.explanation: A motorcycle offers a rider far less protection than a car's structure does, and can be harder for other drivers to spot. A following distance at least as generous as a car's -- often more -- gives a rider more time and space to react safely.

questions.q: Riding with the headlight on at all times (even in daylight) and wearing high-visibility gear helps mainly because:
options: It is only a legal requirement with no safety benefit
It improves the motorcycle's fuel efficiency
A motorcycle's smaller size makes it harder for other drivers to notice, so extra visibility measures reduce the risk of not being seen
It allows the rider to travel faster safely
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's smaller visual profile means other drivers, especially when scanning quickly at junctions, can miss it more easily than a car. Keeping the headlight on and wearing high-visibility/reflective gear makes a rider noticeably easier to spot.

questions.q: To initiate a turn or lean at speed on a motorcycle, a rider uses 'countersteering', which means:
options: Turning the handlebars in the same direction as the intended turn and holding them there
Briefly pushing the handlebar in the opposite direction of the intended turn, which causes the motorcycle to lean and turn that way
Only using body weight, never the handlebars
Braking hard while turning the handlebars
questions.explanation: At riding speed, a brief push on the handlebar opposite to the intended turn direction causes the motorcycle to lean and turn in the intended direction -- the basic mechanism behind steering a two-wheeled vehicle.

questions.q: When motorcyclists ride together in a group, riding in a staggered formation (offset left-right rather than side by side) mainly helps because it:
options: Looks better to other road users
Is required by law in all cases
Gives each rider more space and a clearer view of the road ahead than riding directly side by side
Allows the group to travel faster overall
questions.explanation: A staggered formation increases the space and sightlines between riders compared with riding directly beside one another, reducing the chance of a collision within the group.

questions.q: Worn motorcycle tyre tread is especially dangerous mainly because it:
options: Makes the motorcycle look older
Reduces grip on the road surface, especially in wet conditions, raising the risk of skidding
Only affects fuel economy
Has no effect on braking
questions.explanation: Tread channels water away from the tyre's contact patch; worn tread cannot do this effectively, so grip and control drop sharply on a wet road.

questions.q: Using engine braking (downshifting to a lower gear) as a motorcycle approaches a corner mainly helps because it:
options: Slows the motorcycle smoothly and helps keep it stable, without relying only on the brakes
Increases the motorcycle's top speed
Is required by law before every corner
Has the same effect as applying the front brake alone
questions.explanation: Downshifting smoothly sheds some speed through engine braking, helping keep the motorcycle stable and leaving the rider with brakes still available if needed.

questions.q: A motorcyclist should generally avoid riding directly in the very centre of a traffic lane mainly because:
options: It is against the law to ride in the centre of a lane
The centre position gives the best view of the road
Oil, grease, and debris from other vehicles tend to collect in the centre of a lane, reducing grip there
It makes the rider harder to see
questions.explanation: Fluids and debris dropped by vehicles tend to build up in the centre of a lane, so riding slightly off-centre (while still staying clear of the lane edges) generally gives better grip and visibility.

questions.q: A motorcyclist should check tyre pressure more often and carefully than most car drivers mainly because:
options: Motorcycle tyres are always more expensive
Motorcycle tyres never need checking once fitted
Motorcycles do not have a recommended tyre pressure
A motorcycle balances on only two contact patches, so even a small pressure change has a much bigger effect on handling and stability than in a car
questions.explanation: Because a motorcycle has only two tyre contact patches supporting its balance, incorrect pressure affects handling, stability, and grip far more noticeably than in a four-wheeled vehicle.

questions.q: When carrying luggage on a motorcycle, the load should generally be:
options: Piled as high as possible for maximum space
Kept low, close to the motorcycle's centre, and evenly balanced so it does not upset the bike's handling
Attached loosely so it can shift with the bike's movement
Placed only on one side of the motorcycle
questions.explanation: Luggage carried high, unevenly, or loosely secured shifts the motorcycle's centre of gravity and can seriously affect its handling and balance, especially in corners.

questions.q: Other drivers often misjudge a motorcycle's speed and distance mainly because:
options: Motorcycles are always driven faster than cars
A motorcycle's smaller size and narrower profile make it harder to see and to judge accurately compared with a car
Motorcycles do not have headlights
Motorcyclists always ride in the centre of the lane
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's smaller visual profile makes it genuinely harder for other drivers to judge its speed and distance correctly, which is why extra caution around motorcycles benefits everyone.

questions.q: Parking in front of a fire hydrant or emergency access point is:
options: Allowed for a few minutes
Prohibited at all times
Allowed with hazard lights on
Only prohibited during working hours
questions.explanation: Parking near fire hydrants or emergency access is prohibited at all times to keep access clear for emergency services.

questions.q: Public parking spaces marked in yellow with a wheelchair symbol are reserved for:
options: Any vehicle during off-peak hours
Vehicles displaying a valid disability parking permit
Delivery vehicles only
VIP vehicles
questions.explanation: These marked spaces are legally reserved for vehicles displaying a valid special-needs/disability permit.

questions.q: Paid public parking in most UAE cities generally does not require payment during:
options: Public holidays and specific free hours as posted (e.g., certain evenings/Fridays)
Weekday mornings
Any time - parking is always free
School hours only
questions.explanation: Many paid-parking zones waive charges on public holidays and certain posted free periods, but exact hours vary by emirate and zone.

questions.q: Parking on a yellow-lined kerb generally means:
options: Free parking is allowed
Parking is restricted or prohibited
Parking is only for taxis
Loading zone with no restriction
questions.explanation: Yellow kerb markings typically indicate restricted or prohibited parking, though exact rules are shown on nearby signs.

questions.q: Double parking (parking beside an already parked vehicle, blocking a lane) is:
options: Allowed briefly for loading
Prohibited as it obstructs traffic
Only allowed at night
Allowed for taxis only
questions.explanation: Double parking blocks the flow of traffic and is prohibited under UAE traffic regulations.

questions.q: In Dubai's paid parking system, 'Code A' side-road parking areas allow a maximum short stay of:
options: 1 hour
4 hours
12 hours
24 hours
questions.explanation: Verified in the RTA handbook: Code A refers to side-road parking areas with a short-stay maximum of 4 hours, while Code B parking yards allow up to 24 hours.

questions.q: In Dubai's paid parking system, a 'Code B' parking yard allows a long-stay of up to:
options: 4 hours
8 hours
24 hours
48 hours
questions.explanation: Verified in the RTA handbook: Code B refers to areas specifically created as a parking yard, allowing long stays of up to 24 hours.

questions.q: Non-payment of parking fees or a lost paid-parking ticket in a multi-storey car park carries a fine of:
options: AED 100
AED 150
AED 200
AED 500
questions.explanation: Verified in the RTA handbook's parking violations table: non-payment of the parking fees or a lost ticket (in an MSCP) carries a fine of AED 150.

questions.q: Exceeding the paid parking duration you have paid for carries a fine of:
options: AED 50
AED 100
AED 300
AED 600
questions.explanation: Verified in the RTA handbook's parking violations table: exceeding the paid parking duration carries a fine of AED 100.

questions.q: Parking in a disabled parking bay without the appropriate permit carries a fine of:
options: AED 100
AED 200
AED 500
AED 1000
questions.explanation: Verified in the RTA handbook's parking violations table: parking on a disabled parking space without the appropriate permit carries a fine of AED 500, the highest of the listed parking violations.

questions.q: A 'No Parking' sign means you must not park in the area even if:
options: It is after 10pm
You remain seated in the vehicle
You have hazard lights on
It is raining
questions.explanation: Verified in the RTA handbook: for a 'No Parking' area, you must not park there, even if you are sitting in the vehicle.

questions.q: Before opening a car door after parking, a driver or passenger should:
options: Open it quickly to save time
Check mirrors and look for approaching traffic, cyclists, or pedestrians before opening the door
Only worry about this if parked in a garage
Assume it is always safe if the engine is switched off
questions.explanation: Opening a door without checking can cause a collision with a passing vehicle, cyclist, or pedestrian — always look before opening, especially on the side facing traffic.

questions.q: When reversing your vehicle into a parking space, you should:
options: Rely on the rear-view mirror alone, since it shows everything behind
Reverse quickly to finish before anyone walks behind you
Only use a reversing camera if the vehicle has one, and nothing else
Check all mirrors, glance over your shoulder, and reverse slowly, using a reversing camera or sensors as an aid rather than a replacement for looking
questions.explanation: No single mirror, camera, or sensor shows everything around a reversing vehicle. Combining mirror checks, a shoulder glance, slow speed, and any camera/sensors as an aid gives the best chance of spotting a pedestrian, child, or object in time.

questions.q: When parking on a slope, in addition to applying the handbrake, a driver should generally:
options: Leave the transmission in neutral
Turn the front wheels so that if the vehicle rolls, it moves away from traffic (for example, toward the kerb) and leave it in gear or 'park'
Remove the key from the ignition only, without any other precaution
Leave the engine running
questions.explanation: On a slope, turning the wheels toward the kerb (facing downhill) or away from traffic, and leaving the vehicle in gear ('park' for automatics, a low gear for manuals) in addition to the handbrake, reduces the risk of the vehicle rolling into traffic if the handbrake alone were to fail.

questions.q: Leaving a vehicle's engine running and unattended while parked (for example, to keep the air conditioning on) is generally:
options: Unsafe and inadvisable, since an unattended running vehicle can be stolen, roll away, or pose a fire/carbon-monoxide risk
Always required by law in hot climates
The recommended way to keep passengers cool while shopping
Only a concern if children are inside
questions.explanation: An unattended vehicle with the engine running can be driven off by a thief, can roll if a gear or handbrake fails, and running an engine in an enclosed space risks carbon-monoxide build-up. It is a basic safety habit not to leave a running vehicle unattended.

questions.q: Parking a vehicle too close to a street corner or junction is a hazard mainly because it:
options: Makes the vehicle harder to steal
Blocks the sightlines other drivers and pedestrians need to see approaching traffic at the junction
Is always cheaper than parking elsewhere
Improves traffic flow around the corner
questions.explanation: A vehicle parked right at a corner can hide approaching traffic, pedestrians, or cyclists from each other's view, which is why parking close to junctions is restricted.

questions.q: Parking a vehicle so that it blocks a driveway or another vehicle's exit is a problem mainly because it:
options: Can trap the other vehicle and prevent it leaving, which may be urgent (for example, an emergency)
Is only a minor inconvenience with no real consequence
Is allowed as long as it is only for a few minutes
Improves the appearance of the street
questions.explanation: Blocking a driveway or another vehicle's only way out can prevent someone from leaving when they urgently need to, which is why it is treated as a serious parking violation.

questions.q: When parking on level ground, in addition to applying the handbrake, a driver with a manual transmission vehicle should generally:
options: Leave the transmission in neutral
Remove the key and leave the transmission in any gear
Leave the transmission in gear (or 'Park' for an automatic) as an extra safeguard against the vehicle rolling
Rev the engine before switching it off
questions.explanation: Leaving a manual gearbox in gear, or an automatic in 'Park', adds a mechanical safeguard on top of the handbrake against unwanted vehicle movement.

questions.q: Before opening a car door on the traffic side of the road after parking, a driver or passenger should:
options: Open the door quickly so as not to block traffic for long
Assume no cyclists or vehicles are coming since the vehicle is stationary
Only check the mirror, since a shoulder check is unnecessary
Check mirrors and look back over the shoulder for approaching traffic or cyclists before opening the door
questions.explanation: A door opened suddenly into traffic can cause a serious collision with a passing cyclist or vehicle, so checking mirrors and looking back before opening the door is essential.

questions.q: What must you do after paying at a Dubai parking meter that issues a paper ticket?
options: Keep the ticket in your pocket
Display the ticket visibly on your dashboard
Give the ticket to the nearest RTA officer
Throw the ticket away immediately
questions.explanation: When a parking payment method issues a paper ticket, it must be displayed on the vehicle's dashboard so it is visible for inspection.

questions.q: A Dubai Seasonal Parking Card lets you park in any allowed space without buying a ticket each time. What is true about it?
options: It only works on weekends
Its validity ranges from 90 to 365 days depending on the plan purchased
It can only be used once
It is only for delivery vehicles
questions.explanation: Seasonal Parking Cards are sold in validity periods ranging from 90 days up to 365 days, letting the holder park in any allowed paid zone without a per-visit ticket.

questions.q: When entering a roundabout, a driver must generally give way to:
options: Traffic already circulating in the roundabout from the right
Traffic waiting to enter from other roads
No one, roundabouts have no priority rule
Only buses and trucks
questions.explanation: Vehicles already inside the roundabout, approaching from the right, generally have priority over those entering.

questions.q: To exit a roundabout, a driver should:
options: Never signal
Signal left before taking the exit
Signal right before taking the exit
Stop completely before exiting
questions.explanation: Drivers should indicate left shortly before their exit to warn other road users and pedestrians of their intention.

questions.q: At a signal-controlled intersection turning left with a green arrow, a driver:
options: Must yield to all oncoming traffic regardless of the arrow
May proceed with priority as protected traffic must wait
Should wait for a full green circle instead
Cannot turn left at all
questions.explanation: A green arrow gives a protected turn; opposing traffic is normally held by a red signal during that phase.

questions.q: At a four-way stop intersection with no signals, priority generally goes to:
options: The vehicle that arrived and stopped first
The vehicle turning left
The vehicle on the left
Whoever accelerates fastest
questions.explanation: At an all-way stop, the vehicle that stops first generally proceeds first, with right-of-way rules applying for simultaneous arrivals.

questions.q: When taking the first exit on a roundabout, a driver should generally approach in:
options: The leftmost lane and signal left on approach
The rightmost lane and signal left on approach
Any lane without signalling
The centre lane only
questions.explanation: For the first exit, drivers typically stay in the right-hand lane and signal left as they approach the roundabout.

questions.q: A yellow box junction (grid marking) on the road means:
options: You may stop there if traffic is heavy
Do not enter unless your exit is clear, to avoid blocking the junction
It is a designated parking area
It marks a pedestrian crossing only
questions.explanation: Yellow box markings prevent drivers from entering and blocking an intersection when their exit route is not clear.

questions.q: When travelling around a roundabout in the UAE, you should keep to which side of the central island?
options: The left
The right
Either side, no rule applies
Straddle the centre line
questions.explanation: Verified in the RTA handbook: at a roundabout you should always keep to the right of the central island, travelling around it in an anti-clockwise direction.

questions.q: As you are about to enter a roundabout, you must give way to:
options: Vehicles behind you
Vehicles already in the roundabout approaching from your left
Vehicles waiting at other entrances
Pedestrians only
questions.explanation: Verified in the RTA handbook: once you have selected the correct lane and are about to enter the roundabout, you must give way to all vehicles already in it moving towards you from the left.

questions.q: On a two-lane roundabout, if you intend to turn right, you should:
options: Approach and stay in the left lane
Approach in the right lane and leave in the right-hand lane
Use either lane and switch freely
Enter from the hard shoulder
questions.explanation: Verified in the RTA handbook: for a two-lane roundabout, turning right means approaching in the right lane, staying in it, signalling right, and leaving in the right-hand lane.

questions.q: On a three-lane roundabout, which lane is reserved only for vehicles turning left?
options: The right-hand lane
The centre lane
The left-hand lane
Any lane may be used
questions.explanation: Verified in the RTA handbook: on a three-lane roundabout you should not choose the left-hand lane unless turning left, as that lane is reserved for left-turning vehicles only.

questions.q: At an intersection without signals, where a minor road meets a main road, priority must generally be given to:
options: Whichever vehicle arrives first
Vehicles coming from the main road
Vehicles turning left
The larger vehicle
questions.explanation: Verified in the RTA handbook: at such intersections, priority of crossing must be given to vehicles coming from a main road; where there is a roundabout, priority goes to vehicles already in it.

questions.q: In the UAE, right of way at an intersection with no traffic signals is decided mainly by:
options: Always giving way to the vehicle approaching from your right, in every case
Signs, road markings, and which road is the major/minor road — not an automatic "vehicle on the right" rule
Whichever vehicle is travelling faster
Whichever vehicle arrives first, regardless of signs
questions.explanation: Unlike some countries' blanket "yield to the right" convention, right of way in the UAE is set by the actual signs, road markings, and road hierarchy at that junction (e.g. a GIVE WAY or STOP sign on the minor road) rather than a fixed left/right rule — always follow what the signs and markings actually say. (Flagged for verification against the exact statutory wording, since this is a common source of confusion between different countries' conventions.)

questions.q: When two lanes merge into one because of a lane closure ahead (for example, roadworks), the safer technique is generally to:
options: Merge early and as soon as possible, regardless of the queue in the continuing lane
Use both lanes up to the merge point and take turns merging one vehicle at a time ("zip merging"), rather than everyone crowding into one lane early
Speed up in the closing lane to get ahead of as many vehicles as possible
Stop completely in the closing lane and wait for a gap
questions.explanation: Taking turns merging one-for-one right at the point where a lane actually ends (rather than everyone squeezing into the continuing lane far in advance) uses the road's full capacity and reduces sudden braking and long queues — but it still requires courtesy and should never involve racing another vehicle to the merge point.

questions.q: At a marked pedestrian crossing on the approach to or exit from a roundabout, a driver should:
options: Give way to pedestrians already on or clearly about to use the crossing
Only give way if a police officer is directing traffic
Proceed as normal since roundabout traffic always has priority
Sound the horn to clear pedestrians from the crossing
questions.explanation: A roundabout's circulating traffic having general priority over entering vehicles does not remove a driver's duty to give way to pedestrians at a marked crossing on the approach or exit; pedestrian safety at a crossing always comes first.

questions.q: When sharing a roundabout with a cyclist, a driver should:
options: Overtake the cyclist as quickly as possible inside the roundabout
Expect the cyclist to always take the outer lane
Give the cyclist extra space, since a cyclist may hold a position in the lane rather than hug the kerb for stability and visibility
Sound the horn to encourage the cyclist to move faster
questions.explanation: Cyclists on a roundabout often ride further from the kerb than usual for their own stability and visibility. Drivers should allow extra space and patience rather than trying to squeeze past.

questions.q: At a small painted 'mini-roundabout' (a flat circular marking rather than a raised island), a driver should:
options: Ignore the normal roundabout rules since it is only painted
Still give way to traffic already on the roundabout, approaching from the right, just as at a normal roundabout
Always have priority over traffic already circulating
Stop completely before entering, regardless of traffic
questions.explanation: A mini-roundabout works on the same give-way principle as a full-sized roundabout, even though its island is just a painted marking rather than a raised kerb.

questions.q: On a multi-lane roundabout, a driver should choose the correct lane:
options: Before entering the roundabout, based on the exit they intend to take, rather than changing lanes while inside it
Only after entering the roundabout
At random, since lane choice does not matter
Only if another driver signals to let them change
questions.explanation: Choosing the right lane before entry avoids the need for unsafe lane changes while circulating, which is a common cause of roundabout collisions.

questions.q: An emergency vehicle with sirens and lights on approaches while you are already circulating inside a roundabout. You should:
options: Stop immediately inside the roundabout
Continue to your intended exit, then pull over safely to let the emergency vehicle pass
Reverse to let it through
Speed up to exit before it arrives
questions.explanation: Stopping inside a roundabout blocks other traffic and creates a hazard; the safer approach is to complete the exit you were already taking, then pull over.

questions.q: At a T-junction with no signals, where a minor side road ends at a main through road, priority generally belongs to:
options: Whichever vehicle is larger
Traffic turning right, regardless of which road it is on
Traffic already travelling on the main through road, regardless of the turning direction of the joining vehicle
Whichever vehicle arrives first
questions.explanation: At an unsignalled T-junction, traffic on the continuous main road generally has priority over traffic joining or crossing from the terminating side road.

questions.q: At an intersection controlled by a police officer whose signals conflict with the traffic lights, which do you obey?
options: Always the traffic lights
Always the police officer's signals
Whichever came first
You may choose either
questions.explanation: A police officer directing traffic always overrides automatic traffic signals; their hand signals take precedence over the lights.

questions.q: You are turning left at a junction and see an oncoming vehicle going straight through. Who has priority?
options: You, because you signaled first
The oncoming vehicle going straight, unless signs/signals say otherwise
Whoever is driving a larger vehicle
It is always a 50/50 negotiation
questions.explanation: A vehicle turning across the path of oncoming traffic must normally give way to vehicles coming straight through, unless a sign, signal, or marking states otherwise.

questions.q: A circular blue sign with a white arrow pointing up means:
options: You must turn left
You must go straight ahead only
Parking is allowed
No entry for vehicles
questions.explanation: Blue circular signs with a white arrow show a mandatory direction; an upward arrow means traffic must proceed straight ahead only.

questions.q: A blue circular sign showing a bicycle means:
options: Bicycles are prohibited
This lane is reserved for bicycles only
Cyclists must dismount
Bicycles have no right of way
questions.explanation: A blue circle with a bicycle symbol is a mandatory sign marking a lane reserved exclusively for cyclists.

questions.q: A triangular sign with a red border showing two children means:
options: A playground is ahead with no traffic
School or children crossing area ahead - drive carefully
Children are not allowed on this road
A pedestrian bridge is ahead
questions.explanation: Red-bordered triangular signs warn of hazards ahead; the children symbol warns of a school zone or a place children may cross.

questions.q: A triangular warning sign with a curved arrow indicates:
options: A U-turn is mandatory
A dangerous bend or curve ahead
A roundabout is ahead
Overtaking is allowed
questions.explanation: This warning sign alerts drivers to slow down for a sharp bend or curve in the road ahead.

questions.q: A blue rectangular sign with a white 'P' and a red diagonal line means:
options: Parking is available
Parking is not allowed here
Only police vehicles may park
Paid parking only
questions.explanation: A 'P' with a red diagonal strike is an informatory/prohibitory sign meaning parking is not permitted in that area.

questions.q: A green rectangular sign showing a hospital symbol tells drivers:
options: A hospital zone is ahead where they should reduce noise and speed
Only ambulances may use this road
There is no hospital nearby
U-turns are mandatory here
questions.explanation: Green informatory signs guide drivers to facilities; a hospital symbol also signals a quiet, careful-driving zone nearby.

questions.q: A green sign with a white arrow and 'Abu Dhabi' written on it is:
options: A warning sign
A directional/guide sign showing the route to Abu Dhabi
A mandatory sign
A speed limit sign
questions.explanation: Green directional signs guide drivers toward cities, exits and destinations along the route.

questions.q: A sign showing a white 'H' on a blue background indicates:
options: A helipad or hospital nearby
A highway entrance
A horse-crossing area
A holiday resort
questions.explanation: The 'H' symbol on a blue informatory sign typically points drivers toward a hospital or helipad.

questions.q: A red circle with a white horizontal bar means:
options: Give way ahead
No entry for all vehicles
One-way street
Speed limit ends
questions.explanation: A plain red circle (no other symbol) is the standard 'No Entry' sign forbidding all vehicles from entering.

questions.q: A triangular sign with an exclamation mark (!) generally warns of:
options: A general danger or hazard ahead not covered by a specific symbol
Road works finishing soon
A speed camera
End of a motorway
questions.explanation: The exclamation mark is a general hazard warning used when no specific pictogram exists for the danger ahead.

questions.q: The red octagonal sign with a white border reading "STOP" means:
options: Slow down and proceed if the road looks clear
You must come to a complete stop before proceeding, even if the road looks clear
Give way only to traffic coming from your right
Sound your horn before moving off
questions.explanation: The eight-sided red STOP sign requires every driver to come to a full stop at the marked line or before the intersection, then proceed only when it is safe.

questions.q: A red circular sign with a solid white horizontal bar and no other markings means:
options: No entry for any vehicle from this direction
One-way street ahead
No parking allowed here
The speed limit shown earlier now ends
questions.explanation: This is the international 'No Entry' sign: vehicles must not enter the road from this direction, even though traffic or pedestrians on the other side may still use it.

questions.q: A red-ringed circular sign showing a U-shaped arrow struck through with a red line means:
options: You must not overtake here
You must not make a U-turn at this point
You must not reverse here
You must not park facing either direction
questions.explanation: This is the RTA handbook's 'No U-turn' prohibitory sign: drivers must not turn their vehicle around to face the opposite direction at that location.

questions.q: A circular sign, ringed in red, showing a black car and a red car side by side means:
